overview.description: Forty-One Syrian (also known as '400' or 'Arba'meyeh') is the preeminent partnership trick-taking game of Syria and Lebanon. It is a derivative of Whist that features a unique betting mechanics where Hearts are permanently the trump suit and players must reach a total of exactly 41 points (or 44 in some regions) to win. The game is famous for its '11-point threshold'â€”if the collective bids of all four players don't total at least 11, the hand is declared void and re-dealt, leading to intense tactical bidding and psychological bluffing.

history.origins: Rooted in the Levant region, 400 evolved from Ottoman-era card games. Despite its name '400', the target score is 41, a discrepancy that remains a point of cultural humor among players. It is the most common social game played in Syrian coffee houses.
timeline: Late 19th Century: Variations of Whist adapt in the Ottoman Levant.
1920s: The permanent Heart trump and 41ndpoint scoring become standardized in Damascus and Beirut.
1950s: Modern Arba'meyeh conventions (the 11ndbid rule) are established.
Present: A staple of the Syrian and Lebanese diaspora worldwide, often played at large family gatherings.
history.evolution: The game focuses on individual scoring within a partnership framework, creating a unique dynamic where you help your partner while tracking your own progress toward the 41ndpoint goal.
history.cultural: Commonly played late into the night with tea or coffee, characterized by 'Akl'â€”the act of 'eating' an opponent's card.

setup.players: 4 players in two fixed partnerships (North/South vs East/West).
setup.dealing: Dealt anticlockwise in packets (usually 1-2-2-2-2-2-2). Each player receives 13 cards.

rules.objective: Your partnership wins when one partner's score reaches or exceeds 41 points while the other partner's score is positive. If both partnerships reach this in the same deal, the partnership with the higher total score wins.
rules.gameplay:
1. Lead: Player to the dealer's right leads any card.
2. Must Follow Suit: Players must follow the suit led if possible. If void, they may trump with a Heart or discard.
3. Winning a Trick: The highest Heart played wins. If no Hearts are played, the highest card of the suit led wins.
keyRules: The 11-Rule: This prevents players from being too conservative. If everyone has bad hands, someone MUST bluff a higher bid to reach 11, or the hand is void.
No Extras: Winning more tricks than you bid provides zero extra points.
Winning condition: Partnership wins when one partner reaches 41+ points and the other partner has a positive score; if tied in the same deal, higher total partnership score wins.

strategy.basic: Prioritize your high Hearts. Since they are always trumps, an Ace of Hearts is a guaranteed trick. Use your high trumps to 'bleed' your opponents' Hearts early.
strategy.intermediate: The 11-Bid Bluff: If you are the last bidder (the dealer) and the total bids so far only add up to 8, you MUST bid 3 to make the hand legal. Bid 3 even if your hand is worth 0; the strategy is to try and 'steal' tricks from your partner to avoid the point penalty.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Leading: If an opponent has bid 7 (worth 14 points) and is close to 41, your partnership should completely abandon your own bids and focus entirely on making that opponent go 'down'. Prevent them from taking even a single trick if possible.
tips: Bidding exactly 7 is a common 'power move' because it doubles your score, but the penalty for failing is also doubled.
Keep track of the remaining Hearts. If you have the last Heart, any card you lead in that suit is an automatic win.

list.name: Lebanese 400
list.description: Minimum bid 2 (not 1), maximum 12. Different point scale: 2-4 tricks = same as bid; 5=10, 6=12, 7=14, 8=16, 9=27, 10=30, 11=33, 12=36; bid 13 and take all tricks wins whole game. Optional: at 30-39 score must bid at least 3, at 40-49 at least 4, at 50+ at least 5.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Point scale and bid limits are rule-set changes; engine.constants could be overridden when implementing this variant.

list.name: Target 44
list.description: Some play to a target score of 44 rather than 41.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Target score is overridden above; no further explanation needed.

list.name: Bid total 12 when 30+
list.description: Some require that the bids must add up to at least 12 (rather than 11) if any player has a score of 30 or more.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Conditional bid threshold is a rule variant not expressed as a simple constant override.

difficulty.easy: Fails to bid enough to reach the 11ndpoint threshold; forgets Hearts are trumps; doesn't help partner.
difficulty.medium: Bids conservatively (3-5 tricks); protects its own bid above all else; understands basic trump-pulling strategy.
difficulty.hard: Expertly bluffs the 11th bid to force a round; calculates the perfect moment to bid 7 for a double-point win; sabotages opponents approaching 41 with precision leading.

considerations: AI must handle the 'Anticlockwise' dealing and playing flow which is rare in Western card games.

deal.description: Dealer distributes all 52 cards anticlockwise in packets, 13 to each player.

play_card.description: Play a single card to the trick.
play_card.constraints: Must follow suit if possible. If void in suit, may trump (Hearts) or discard.

discard.description: Play a card that does not follow suit and is not a trump (when void in both).
discard.constraints: Only legal if void in the suit led and have no Hearts.

bid.description: State the number of tricks you think you can take (1 to 13). Bid value: 1-6 = points equal to bid; 7+ = double points. Total of all four bids must be at least 11 or the hand is void.
bid.constraints: One bid per player per hand, starting with player to dealer's right, anticlockwise. Minimum bid 1.

go_out.reason: Game has no going out mechanic.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Highest heart wins trick; if no hearts, highest card of suit led wins.

trickConfig.leadRestrictions: Player to dealer's right leads first; winner of each trick leads next.

engine.deckDescription: One full deck of 52 cards using French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) and standard ranks from ace through king, with no jokers.
engine.suitDescription: French suits: hearts (cœurs), diamonds (carreaux), clubs (trèfles), and spades (piques). Each suit has thirteen cards from ace through king.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranking for a 52-card deck: ace (high or low by context), king, queen, jack, 10, 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. Thirteen cards per suit.
engine.dealPattern: 13 cards per player, anticlockwise, all cards dealt

hero.title: FORTY-ONE SYRIAN
hero.subtitle: The Levantine Partnership Classic
hero.tagline: Bid. Hearts are trump. Race to 41 points.

synthesis.shortDescription: A Middle Eastern partnership trick-taking game with a unique bidding system where Hearts are permanently trump and the total bid must exceed 11.

prompts.human: Welcome to Forty-One Syrian (400/Arba'meyeh). Each player receives 13 cards. Bid the tricks you can win. Remember: Hearts are always trump. Total bids must be at least 11. Bid 1-6: win points equal to bid. Bid 7+: win double points. Fail your bid: lose points. Your partnership wins when one partner reaches 41+ and the other has a positive score.
prompts.ai: Game: Forty-One Syrian / 400 (Partnership trick-taking). Setup: 4 players, 13 cards each, anticlockwise dealing. Trump: Hearts (permanent). Bidding: Each player bids 1-13 tricks. Win condition: First player to exactly 41 points wins the game. Trick play: Follow suit or trump; highest Heart or highest card of suit led wins.

scoring.description: Points awarded based on tricks won and bid accuracy. First team to 41+ wins. Bidding determines scoring multipliers.
scoring.winCondition: Partnership wins when one partner's score reaches or exceeds 41 points and the other partner's score is positive. If both partnerships reach this in the same deal, the partnership with the higher total score wins.

penalties.Bid_Failed: Lose points equal to bid amount (e.g., bid 6 = -6 points if failed)
penalties.Double_Bid_Failed: Lose double points if 7-bid fails (-14 points)

scoring.splitRules: In partnerships, team points combined. First team to 41+ cumulative points wins.

nullReasons.targetScore: Game does not use target score.
nullReasons.scoringDirection: Game does not use scoring direction.
nullReasons.cardValues: Points come from bid success and tricks won, not from individual card point values.
